subject: Network acceptance checklist & deep dive — on-prem performance go/no-go
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@saasco.com>, Network Ops <netops@saasco.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-12-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Network acceptance checklist & deep dive — on-prem performance go/no-go

Hi Alice,

Thanks for the call earlier — short recap and proposed acceptance criteria so we can align on the network validation window.

Recap (from today's discovery):
- Target SLOs: p95 end-to-end latency <= 250ms for streaming responses up to ~1024 tokens.
- Concurrency: target steady-state 500 concurrent streaming sessions; burst to 1,200 for 2–5min allowed.
- Throughput: sustained 60 requests/sec per deployment region; peak spikes up to 200 req/s for short bursts.
- Egress/bandwidth: estimate ~380–450 Mbps per GPU pool during steady streaming (depends on token lengths).
- Expected KV cache warm-hit behavior: 70% warm-hit expected after 12–15 minutes of steady traffic.

Immediate asks to prepare our validation tests:
1) Network diagram (VPCs, NATs, transit gateways, firewalls) + public IP ranges for peering.
2) Known MTU constraints or GRE overlay that could fragment packets.
3) Typical VPN throughput and any per-tunnel concurrency limits.
4) Scheduled maintenance windows / firewall change lead times.

Attachments referenced: draft-network-test-plan.csv (see stub attached) and sample-runbook.md — will push the formal test plan once we get the diagram.

Proposed acceptance criteria (draft):
- Streaming p95 from client -> Redwood -> model -> client <= 250ms for 95% of test runs across 3 regions.
- Drop in model p95 vs baseline <= 10% during peak simulated concurrency.
- No packet loss >0.1% and TCP retransmit under 1% during steady-state.

Next steps:
- If you can send the network diagram + CIDRs today we'll provision a short-lived peering and run a 2-hour validation window next Wed (12/15) morning PST.
- I'll loop in Karthik (solutions) and Connor (infra) to own the test harness and metrics collection.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Attachment: draft-network-test-plan.csv (stub)
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@saasco.com>

Date: 2027-12-14T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Network acceptance checklist & deep dive — on-prem performance go/no-go

Marissa,

Thanks for the summary — confirmed and attached our current network diagram (saasco-onprem-network-diagram.pdf).

Quick answers:
- CIDR ranges for our egress: 54.210.0.0/16, 18.196.0.0/16 (public NATs). We also have a dedicated transit CIDR 10.100.0.0/16 for peering traffic.
- We're using an on-prem VPN concentrator with aggregated throughput of ~750 Mbps; single-tunnel average ~400 Mbps.
- We do have an intermediate firewall that performs DPI; expect an extra 5–15ms of processing per packet during inspection-heavy flows.
- MTU is 1500 on the edge; there is a legacy overlay on a subset of hosts with egress MTU 1400.

Attachments: saasco-onprem-network-diagram.pdf (stub)

We'll confirm maintenance windows — Wed morning PST looks doable but can we do an afternoon slot (start 13:00 PST) to align with our network ops staffing?

Best,

Alice Nguyen
Head of Platform Engineering | SaaSCo
alice.nguyen@saasco.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-12-14T12:00:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Network acceptance checklist — proposed test plan & acceptance criteria

Karthik / Connor — forwarding Alice's diagram. Below is the proposed test plan and clear acceptance criteria we should present tomorrow:

Planned validation window: 2027-12-15 13:00–15:00 PST (2 hours)

Test plan (high level):
- Steady-state throughput ramp: ramp to 60 req/s over 10 minutes; hold for 40 minutes.
- Concurrency soak: spin 500 concurrent streaming sessions for 30 minutes; monitor p95 and packet retransmits.
- Spike test: burst to 1,200 concurrent sessions for 3 minutes; measure error rates and tail latency.
- Packet path test: run traceroutes and mtr from our egress to their provided CIDRs; capture per-hop latency.
- MTU/fragmentation check: send MTU-sized payload stream to detect fragmentation-induced latency.

Metrics to capture:
- Client->Redwood one-way and round-trip breakdown (we'll instrument TCP handshake + TLS timing).
- Token-level generation time and first-byte latency (streaming FBL).
- TCP retransmits, packet loss, and jitter.

Proposed latency budget (p95 target <= 250ms):
- Client network + browser/frontend: 50ms
- Edge/cloud egress + transit: 30–40ms
- On-prem VPN/firewall overhead: 5–20ms (per Alice)
- Redwood processing/model p95 target: 140–165ms
Total (budgeted): 225–275ms (aim to be <=250ms in 95% of runs)

Fail conditions (immediate):
- p95 > 300ms for streaming FBL during steady-state
- >1% request error rate or >5% dropped streams during spike tests
- TCP retransmit >1%

Attachments for test run (stubs): network-validation-runbook.md, acceptance-checklist.md, test-results-template.csv

I'll draft the formal runbook and push to the shared Drive link below. After the tests, if behavior is acceptable we'll open the SOW and finalize the Dedicated capacity sizing.

-Marissa
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@saasco.com>

Also attaching a minimal config export (firewall-config-export.txt) to highlight the DPI policy applied to the transit path.

Thanks — see you Wed.

Alice
